criteria.criterion: Bally's pays for employee memberships in the Upwards network
criteria.promise_scope: Promisor: Bally's. Intended beneficiaries: Bally's employees. Location: unspecified in the quoted promise passage. Benefit/action promised or reported in the original terms: Bally's says it funds every employee membership to the Upwards network; related excerpts describe this as paying for employees' membership in Upwards. Material conditions: the memberships are the mechanism tied to childcare access/priority benefits, but the promise text itself is about funding memberships, not proving each employee used them.
criteria.observed_scope: Bally’s self-reports that it funds every employee membership to the Upwards network; beneficiary population is employees, with no companywide location stated in c1 and a separate reference in c3 to including Bally’s Bronx employees; benefit established is funded Upwards memberships. Actual individual enrollment or availability to employees at every proposed site is not specified.
criteria.explanation: The observed outcomes include Bally’s direct present-tense statement, "We fund every employee membership to the Upwards network," which is evidence of the reported practice of paying for employee memberships. A related passage also says Bally’s partnered with Upwards "to offer high-quality childcare options including for Bally’s Bronx employees," which supports that Bronx employees are among the intended beneficiaries. These passages establish the organization’s self-reported funding of employee Upwards memberships, but they do not identify which employees are enrolled or independently verify access for all employees at every site.

delivery_support.quote: We fund every employee membership to the Upwards network and offer financial assistance to ease the burden of childcare costs. This includes contributing to a Dependent Care FSA or providing "credits" for free childcare days.
we have partnered with Upwards, the largest childcare network in the United States, to offer high-quality childcare options including for Bally’s Bronx employees.

criteria.fulfilled_part: Bally’s reports that it funds every employee membership to the Upwards network for its employees; c3 indicates this includes Bally’s Bronx employees.

criteria.criterion: Those Upwards memberships provide employees priority childcare placement
criteria.promise_scope: Promisor: Bally's. Intended beneficiaries: Bally's employees receiving Upwards memberships. Location: unspecified in the requested query; c2 refers to facilities near Bally's proposed sites. Benefit/action promised: the paid Upwards memberships would give employees priority childcare placement at Upwards facilities. Material conditions: this is priority eligibility/placement benefit through membership, not proof that employees obtained childcare slots.
criteria.observed_scope: Bally’s self-reports that Upwards members receive priority placement at Upwards facilities. Beneficiaries actually established are members; because v1 reports Bally’s funds employee memberships, this supports that employee members would receive that membership benefit. Location is tied only to facilities "near our proposed sites," not to a specific sitewide proof of usable access. Benefit established is priority placement as a membership feature, not actual childcare slots obtained.
criteria.explanation: The observed outcomes state, "Members also receive priority placement at Upwards facilities," which directly supports that priority placement is a feature of Upwards membership. Read together with Bally’s report that it funds every employee membership to the Upwards network, this supports delivery of memberships that provide employees priority placement eligibility. The evidence does not show that employees actually obtained childcare placements or that priority placement was usable at every proposed site, but the condition here is the provision of priority placement through membership, not successful slot placement.

delivery_support.quote: Members also receive priority placement at Upwards facilities, which are plentiful near our proposed sites, and the program is increasingly popular among our employees.

Cited source excerpts (promise, delivery, or context as assessed above):
c1: “We fund every employee membership to the Upwards network and offer financial assistance to ease the burden of childcare costs. This includes contributing to a Dependent Care FSA or providing "credits" for free childcare days.”
https://nycasinos.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/09/ballys-amendment-to-rfa-response-form_september-28-2025.pdf

c2: “Members also receive priority placement at Upwards facilities, which are plentiful near our proposed sites, and the program is increasingly popular among our employees.”
https://nycasinos.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/09/ballys-amendment-to-rfa-response-form_september-28-2025.pdf

c3: “To assist our working families, we have partnered with Upwards, the largest childcare network in the United States, to offer high-quality childcare options including for Bally’s Bronx employees.”
https://nycasinos.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/09/ballys-amendment-to-rfa-response-form_september-28-2025.pdf

c4: “Bally’s committed to pay for employees’ membership in Upwards, which would give the employee priority childcare placement in Upwards’ vetted facilities, but little information was provided about what membership entails or whether Upwards’ network facilities are already at capacity.”
https://nycasinos.ny.gov/gaming-facility-location-board-final-report-and-findings-march-2026

c5: “The Board recommends the Commission require Bally’s to provide annual updates on employee participation in the Upwards membership program for childcare and to address any challenges employees face in accessing convenient daycare options.”
https://nycasinos.ny.gov/gaming-facility-location-board-final-report-and-findings-march-2026

c6: “Childcare Services: Free childcare support for employees through our Upwards partnership”
https://nycasinos.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/07/evalloc4.ballys.communities_redacted.pdf
